\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HermiteDefinitions}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Normalized Hermite polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p012-b001}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial}
\leanok
For each integer $k\ge 0$, let $H_k$ be the $k$th Gaussian Hermite polynomial. The
normalized Hermite polynomial is $H_k/\sqrt{k!}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Multivariate Hermite polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p012-b001}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial}
Let $n\ge 0$ and let $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$ be a tuple of nonnegative
integers. The multivariate Hermite polynomial indexed by $\alpha$ is the product
$\prod_{i=1}^n H_{\alpha_i}(x_i)/\sqrt{\alpha_i!}$, where $H_j/\sqrt{j!}$ is the
normalized Gaussian Hermite polynomial of degree $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hermite function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p012-b001}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $\alpha$ assign a nonnegative integer to each of the $n$ coordinates,
and let $x\in\mathbb R^n$. The Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$ is the value at $x$
of the multivariate Hermite polynomial indexed by $\alpha$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hermite coefficient]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p012-b001}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $\alpha$ assign a nonnegative
integer to each coordinate. The Hermite coefficient of $f$ at $\alpha$ is the integral
of $f(x)$ times the Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$, with respect to the product of
$n$ standard Gaussian measures.
\end{definition}
